einzeiler: A deep dive into the 2014 cult classic thriller The Guest starring Dan Stevens.
kurzfassung: The hosts examine the 2014 thriller The Guest, highlighting its status as a genuine cult classic that helped launch Dan Stevens' movie career. They discuss the film's 1980s aesthetic, its clever homage to John Carpenter movies, and its darkly comedic premise involving a dangerously unhinged visitor. Finally, they break down the opening scenes and character dynamics before steering listeners toward their Patreon for the full episode.
stichpunkte: Discussion of unexpected physical transformations and roles in various film projects by Dan Stevens
Analysis of The Guest as a true cult classic that struggled initially at the box office before finding its audience over a decade
Comparison of modern 1980s nostalgia in cinema versus how the film places its retro atmosphere directly into the present day
Appreciation for the soundtrack choices, including obscure John Carpenter-style tracks and Sisters of Mercy
Visual and thematic nods to the Halloween franchise, particularly Season of the Witch and Halloween 4
The central comedic irony of a super-soldier trying to help a grieving family while being entirely unhinged
Breakdown of the opening sequence featuring the arrival of the mysterious visitor at the Peterson family home

clips.hook: That's not how this cult classic thing works!
clips.text: True cult classics often take years to find their audience after initially bombing at the box office with zero commercial splash.

clips.hook: Setting 80s nostalgia in the present day!
clips.text: A good genre movie improves on standard nostalgia tropes by placing an 80s aesthetic directly into a modern setting rather than setting the story in the past.

clips.hook: What if Michael Myers tried to be a good guy?
clips.text: The entire premise of the film functions like a slasher villain attempting to help a family while remaining completely broken in the head.

clips.hook: When do you finally take down the dead son altar?
clips.text: Keeping a deceased relative's memorial shrine intact a year later makes for an awkward living situation when random strangers drop by.

You're listening to an extended preview of our September WLM on The Guest! To access the full, commercial-free show, click through to our Patreon and sign up now!
“I love this sad sack shit” - Eric on the father in this movie

On the first We ❤️ Movies episode of season 17, we’re chatting about a total all-timer cult classic, Adam Wingard’s The Guest!

Is this the single best Dan Stevens performance we’ve seen so far? How incredible is this soundtrack and score combo? Is this family too into Halloween? Is Leland Orser’s character the biggest “loser dad” guy in a while? Was there ever a man cooler than Lance Reddick—especially when he was wearing boss-ass dusters like the one he sports in this film? And who hasn’t known a townie scum bag like old Craig here? PLUS: That poor, elderly couple just wanted to celebrate their wedding anniversary at that quiet diner!
The Guest stars Dan Stevens, Maika Monroe, Brendan Meyer, Sheila Kelley, Leland Order, Chase Williamson, Joel David Moore, Ethan Emery, Tabatha Shaun, AJ Bowen, and the late, great Lance Reddick as Major Carver; directed by Adam Wingard.
